original_test_intent: Verify the Type 7 Supported SRAM Type bitmask for each cache instance advertises the approved set of SRAM implementation modes, uses defined/reserved bits correctly, contains the reported Current SRAM Type and persists after reboot.
original_method: Capture complete raw/decoded Type 7 records, retain the supported-type UINT16 per handle/level, decode all defined bits with applicable SMBIOS definitions, compare with the approved cache technology set and Current SRAM Type mask, reboot and repeat.
manual_activity: A user approves supported SRAM sets, SMBIOS bit definitions, unknown/other/reserved policy and reboot plan. Bitmask collection and comparison are automatable.
required_inputs: Expected supported SRAM type set for each Type 7 handle/level
Applicable SMBIOS bit assignments and reserved-bit mask
Policy for `Other`, `Unknown`, multiple supported modes and zero masks
Expected Current SRAM Type and requirement that current defined bits are supported
Validated raw/decoded parser plus approved reboot and OOB recovery plan
safety_requirements: Read SMBIOS only; do not change cache technology, modes, CPU settings or firmware.
Preserve the raw 16-bit support mask and all set reserved/unknown bits; decoded label lists are insufficient.
Treat this as a capability set, not necessarily the active SRAM implementation; validate Current SRAM Type separately as a subset/approved relationship.
Do not infer a physical SRAM circuit technology from generic OS cache data.
Stop on reserved-bit violations, unsupported current bits, per-cache ambiguity, drift or reboot failure; no automatic retry.
agent_execution_scope: Collect and decode Supported SRAM Type per cache handle, preserve unknown bits, compare approved capability sets and Current SRAM relationship before/after reboot.
Do not alter cache modes, invent technology mappings or decide PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve supported/current SRAM bitsets and unknown/other/reserved handling.
Approve reboot/recovery and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The label is correct, but grep loses raw mask, handle/level and reserved bits and cannot verify Current SRAM Type is within the supported set.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Archive complete raw/decoded Type 7 records, extract supported and current SRAM masks per handle and emit defined/reserved bitsets plus subset checks.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Supported SRAM Type scope, Type 7 script and 5/5-minute values are retained.

modernized_recommendation.status: SRAM CAPABILITY BITSET AND CURRENT-SUBSET VALIDATION
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Decode the raw supported mask with the applicable SMBIOS table, retain unknown/reserved bits, bind by Type 7 handle and verify the approved Current SRAM Type relationship before and after reboot.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record SMBIOS, BIOS, CPU/cache design and parser/dmidecode versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Applicable SMBIOS Type 7 Supported SRAM Type and Current SRAM Type bit definitions, approved processor/cache documentation and installed tool documentation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds raw capability-set, reserved-bit and supported-versus-current validation.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; detects internally inconsistent cache technology metadata that a label-only comparison misses.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: SMBIOS terminology is historical and coarse; it should be validated as firmware metadata rather than mapped to modern microarchitecture without vendor evidence.

project_override_considerations: A project may approve multiple supported modes or explicit Unknown/Other bits by cache instance, but must define the raw bitset and ensure the current mask is not an unadvertised technology.
expected_evidence: Approved supported/current SRAM matrix, SMBIOS bit definitions, reserved policy and tool versions
Complete pre-reboot Type 7 table with handle/level, raw supported mask and decoded defined/unknown bits
Current SRAM raw mask and supported-subset/policy result per cache
Approved reboot/health evidence and equivalent post-reboot comparison
Engineer verdict with rationale for any Unknown/Other bit

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source consistently targets a defined Type 7 capability bitmask; expected technology sets are project inputs.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The mask is safely readable and machine-decodable once the approved bit policy is supplied.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Adds raw mask, cache identity, reserved-bit retention and current-type relationship.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Keeps version-aware bitset analysis while correcting capability to FULLY AUTOMATABLE and adding the current-subset invariant.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates supported capability from active current type and avoids unsupported OS/microarchitecture substitution.

review_improvement: Detects current SRAM bits that firmware never advertises as supported and preserves ambiguous legacy `Unknown`/`Other` semantics for engineering review.
independent_technical_reasoning: With approved bit definitions and expected sets, raw extraction, bitset decoding, subset checks and reboot persistence are deterministic software operations.
